init.title: Furbo options
init.description: How often to poll the Furbo cloud, and whether to poll the pet calendar for events and daily activity. The next pages cover each camera's live video and local bridge.

camera.title: Live video and controls for {name}
camera.description: Furbo streams and takes commands over a proprietary P2P protocol that Home Assistant cannot speak directly. Run the Furbo P2P bridge on a machine on the camera's LAN: publish its video through go2rtc and enter the RTSP URL, and run its HTTP API (furbo_p2p.py serve) and enter that URL for camera controls. Leave a field empty to skip it.

data_description.stream_url: For example rtsp://furbo:PASSWORD@192.168.1.10:8554/furbo (the add-on's RTSP is password-protected). Accepted schemes: rtsp, rtsps, http, https. Creates the camera entity.
data_description.bridge_url: For example http://192.168.1.10:8791. Enables camera power, volume, night vision, bark sensitivity, tracking, pan and treat toss.
data_description.bridge_token: The value given to furbo_p2p.py serve --token. The bridge requires it.

error.invalid_stream_url: Enter an rtsp://, rtsps://, http:// or https:// URL, or leave the field empty.
error.invalid_bridge_url: Enter an http:// or https:// URL, or leave the field empty.

bridge_needs_code.title: Furbo Bridge needs a verification code
bridge_needs_code.description:
The Furbo Bridge add-on could not sign in to Furbo: the cloud is asking for a verification code, and only you can supply one. Until it can sign in, the add-on cannot hand Home Assistant a fresh token, so Furbo will keep asking you to sign in again, and the camera will stop working once its current session drops.

To fix it: in the add-on's configuration turn **reset_session** on and restart the add-on. If it is already on, turn it off, restart, then turn it on again. Watch the add-on log for the message saying a code has been emailed, put that code in **mfa_code**, and restart the add-on once more. This notice clears by itself once the add-on can hand over a token again.
